questions.question: 1. The expression for shear strength in a double shear test is

explanations.a: Incorrect. This expression corresponds to single shear.
explanations.b: Correct. In double shear, the resisting area is twice the specimen cross-sectional area.
explanations.c: Incorrect. This would overestimate the shear strength.
explanations.d: Incorrect. This expression does not represent stress.

questions.question: 2. The shear stress measured in a direct shear test is

explanations.a: Correct. The specimen is directly subjected to shear loading.
explanations.b: Incorrect. Bending stress arises from bending moments.
explanations.c: Incorrect. Thermal stress is caused by temperature changes.
explanations.d: Incorrect. Residual stress is unrelated to the applied shear load in this test.

questions.question: 3. Shear strength is an important design property for

explanations.a: Incorrect. This is only one application.
explanations.b: Incorrect. This is only one application.
explanations.c: Incorrect. This is only one application.
explanations.d: Correct. Shear strength is important in all these engineering applications.

questions.question: 4. Modulus of rigidity is directly determined from a standard double shear test.

explanations.a: Incorrect. A standard double shear test is used to determine shear strength, not modulus of rigidity.
explanations.b: Correct. Modulus of rigidity is typically determined from torsion-related experiments.

questions.question: 5. A specimen fails under a load of 24 kN in double shear. If the cross-sectional area is 100 mm², the shear strength is

explanations.a: Incorrect. The doubled resisting area must be considered.
explanations.c: Incorrect. This overestimates the shear strength.
explanations.d: Incorrect. This underestimates the shear strength.

questions.question: 6. In double shear, the resisting area compared to single shear is

explanations.a: Incorrect. Double shear increases the resisting area.
explanations.b: Incorrect. The resisting area is not the same.
explanations.c: Correct. Two shear planes provide twice the resisting area.
explanations.d: Incorrect. The increase is not fourfold.

questions.question: 7. A circular specimen has a diameter of 10 mm. Its cross-sectional area is

explanations.d: Incorrect. This is not the correct circular area.

questions.question: 8. A 12 mm diameter specimen fails under a double shear load of 40 kN. The shear strength is closest to

explanations.a: Incorrect. The value is too low.
explanations.c: Incorrect. The resisting area has been neglected.
explanations.d: Incorrect. This greatly overestimates the result.

questions.question: 9. Why is double shear often preferred in engineering connections?

answers.c: It increases the effective resisting area
answers.d: It changes ductile materials into brittle materials

explanations.c: Correct. Double shear provides two resisting planes and increases load-carrying capacity.
explanations.d: Incorrect. Shear conditions do not change material type.
